lots.what_it_is: Large three-section illuminated ceramic Christmas tree in the Atlantic Mold style: glossy green glaze with dark streaking, tiered top, wide skirt tier, and a white base moulded and hand painted as wrapped presents with a toy train. Coloured plastic peg bulbs including red and blue bird shapes; cord attached. No mould mark visible (underside not shown), so possibly an unmarked hobby-ceramic tree rather than genuine Atlantic Mold.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 (whole tree) and photo 2 (close-up of branches) re-checked. Three parts visible: top tree, skirt tier, white presents-and-train base; cord exits the base at right. Bird bulbs in red and blue plus round and flame pegs in red, orange, yellow, green and blue. No chips, cracks or missing pegs seen on the visible faces; no star topper visible. No mark, signature or date can be read anywhere; base underside not photographed. Base painting looks hand done, typical of 1970s-80s hobby ceramics classes. Size not stated.
lots.condition: Looks clean and complete on the visible faces; no obvious chips or repairs. Electrics untested. Back of tree, underside and mark not shown; check every peg is present and the sections sit together without cracks.
lots.score_reason: A popular nostalgic collectable type; verified US auction results for large lit ceramic trees cluster about US$50 to US$110 (A$72 to A$158), with outliers to US$200. Unusual presents-and-train base may help, but no mark is visible and there is no Australian sales record, so mid band.

lots.working: No exact match (presents-and-train base not found sold). Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD in similar condition within 24 months is US$50 (24 inch multi-section tree, some pegs missing, untested, DejaVu 5 Oct 2026) = A$72; 72 / 1.22 = 59, rounded down to $55. Excluded from the floor: US$32 (crazing and discolouration, worse), US$28 (size and condition unknown), the two US$80 repaired trees. Flip: likely resale about A$115 (middle of verified clean results US$75 to US$105, A$108 to A$151); sold locally by pickup only because it is bulky and fragile, so no postage; allow eBay-style 13% fees (A$15) giving A$100 net; 100 / 2.44 = 41, rounded down to $40. Thin margin and a small Australian market.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification of the type is clear, but no maker mark is visible (rule: unread mark means Low), height is unknown and all sold evidence is US auctions converted to AUD; no Tasmanian or Australian comparable.

lots.what_it_is: Seven timber cupboard doors and panels (four routed cathedral-arch doors with porcelain knobs and brass hinges, three loose panels), titled as Huon pine. Species not confirmed: at least one door has dark knots with reddish rings typical of radiata or Baltic pine. The routed arch style is typical of 1980s-90s kitchen joinery.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo re-checked; crop of the third door from left enlarged: it shows two dark knots and broad, wavy grain consistent with radiata pine rather than the fine, knot-light grain usual in Huon pine. Doors 1 and 2 are a honey-gold varnish, door 4 has lost its finish and is water-stained, the loose panels are deeper orange. No stamps or marks; lot tag only.
lots.condition: Used salvage: surface wear, old varnish, staining and finish loss on the right-hand door; hinges and knobs still attached on some. Sizes not stated.
lots.score_reason: If genuine Huon pine, local woodworkers and restorers pay modest sums for salvage (Gowans: Huon panelling boards $45, sets of 4 Huon sash windows $145 to $220). Species doubtful from the photo and routed 1980s-90s doors are less wanted, so likely A$30 to A$80.
